input.covers: goto, then javascript, then uri in PDF order: document work runs inline and the navigation and URI thunks fire after it, in node order.

input.name: a-document-failure-drops-deferred-work
input.covers: A failed document node skips later document nodes (javascript, reset-form, hide) and drops every deferred thunk; the result is partial.

input.name: policy-matrix-defaults
input.covers: The default rows: a lifecycle uri reports, a hover submit blocks, a lifecycle Print blocks, launch and the other fixed types are never executable, recognized types without an interpreter and unknown types are no-executor; canExecute mirrors the root decision.

input.name: a-print-typed-node-uses-the-print-row
input.covers: A node whose type is literally "print" finds policy.print by key, and with no executor is no-executor.

input.name: policy-overrides
input.covers: config.policy rows replace the defaults: block and report refuse with their names, allow executes even for a lifecycle uri.

input.name: policy-rows-merge-and-update-live
input.covers: config.policy merges row-wise over the defaults (a partial row keeps the other origins); getSettings returns the effective policy; updateSettings merges policy rows, and an empty settings patch preserves them for later dispatches.

input.name: execute-named
input.covers: executeNamed runs one Named verb as a user-origin api action through the same queue; a partial context overrides the origin, source or event; Print goes through the adapter door.

input.name: get-action-tree
input.covers: readActionTree reads the raw tree behind each source kind: an annotation (activate by default, or the named /AA event; the /A-shadows-U rule is not applied), a field by object number (not the first numbered field) or by name, a page (open by default or close), and the catalog (OpenAction by default, or the Table-200 tree for a verb). Anything absent is null; the required actions service returns an empty catalog for the second document.
input.reason: Pins what the dispatcher answers: read trees, refusals, and which installed sink or resolver is current, through call outcomes, adapter callbacks and engine calls. Its dispatched actions are compared; the state they build is not.

input.name: uri-without-an-adapter

input.name: named-print-goes-to-the-adapter
input.covers: The Named Print verb reaches the adapter with no context, never the named executor; other named verbs use the executor.

input.name: print-refusals
